page.overview:
Who is Jean Behra?

Jean Marie Behra (born 6 February 1921 in Nice, Alps-Maritimes, Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur, France – died 1 August 1959 at the AVUS, in West Berlin, West Germany) was a French racing driver who competed in Formula One the 1950s.

Originally racing motorcycles, Behra switched full-time to four wheels in , and won two non-championship races that year, alongside a podium at his first race, the . After three years racing with , in he moved to , continuing to win non-championship races, but despite five podiums in , a full World Championship win eluded him.

In he raced for the team, scoring a pair of points finishes alongside a host of retirements, while racing for in sports car races. In he made the move to , partnering Brit Tony Brooks. This however, was only to last a few months as disagreements within the team saw Behra punch two Ferrari personnel, including team manager Romolo Tavoni, and he was fired from the team.

Behra, in association with , was to use his car at the next race, the 1959 German Grand Prix. However, in a sports car race that preceded the Grand Prix race, Behra suffered a horrendous accident as he spun off on the banking and hit a flag pole, suffering fatal skull fractures. The funeral was held six days later in both Berlin and Paris, and he was buried in Nice. Reflecting their ruined relationship, Enzo Ferrari didn't attend the funeral.
